hints_cache: This is a classic parsing problem. Think of it like a calculator where commas are 'addition' (union) and side-by-side expressions are 'multiplication' (concatenation).
Since the expression has nested braces, you can use a Stack or Recursion. A Stack is great for keeping track of your 'current' set of words while you dive into a deeper level of braces.
Try to process the string character by character. You'll need to handle four cases: a letter, a comma, an opening brace, and a closing brace. Each one changes how you combine your current words.

Use a Hash Table (or Set) at each level to automatically handle duplicates. When you hit a comma, it means you've finished one part of a union; when you hit a closing brace, you've finished an entire group that needs to be multiplied with whatever came before it.

Maintain a stack of 'groups' and 'current' word sets. A new brace pushes a fresh state; a comma saves the current set into the group; a closing brace flattens that group into a single set and concatenates it with the level below. Finally, sort the unique results.
